reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Circuit court petition and request for commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12456, A.L. 1945 p. 852; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Covers the right of owners of land to be drained or protected to file a circuit court petition when landowners fail to agree on improvement location, land value, or damages, sets required petition allegations and property descriptions, and requires a prayer for appointment of commissioners to report and recommend adjustments.

headings.title: Rough plat and prior written compensation tender
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers filing a rough plat of affected lands and approximate improvement course (which need not be made by an engineer) with the petition, and the proviso requiring prior written tender of estimated land value, accruing damages, and needed crossing costs to crossed landowners and stating the tender and amount in the petition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and RSMo 1939/1945 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked disagreement prerequisites, required petition allegations and commissioner prayer in (1), and rough plat plus prior written compensation tender proviso in (2). Retained both drafted headings as accurate and concise.

headings.title: Filing petition, naming defendants, and service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12457, A.L. 1945 p. 852, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070), and case annotation (Dillen v. Remley, 327 S.W.2d 931 (1959), on circuit court jurisdiction where lands lie in an adjoining-county chapter 242 district). Covers filing in the circuit clerk's office where affected land is situated, naming non-signing owners of damaged or benefitted land as party defendants, summons and petition service as in ordinary civil actions, and nonresident service under the Missouri civil code.

headings.title: Hearing date, notice, and filing objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and 1959 case annotation. Covers setting an objections hearing date not more than twenty days from the return date, notice accompanying the petition stating its purpose and objection right, filing objections on or before the hearing date and before the hearing hour, and limiting objections to denials of petition allegations.

headings.title: Hearing objections and appointing sworn commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and 1959 case annotation. Covers prompt circuit court hearing of objections and, if overruled, appointment of three disinterested county residents (not kin within the second degree of consanguinity to any affected landowner) who must be sworn before performing chapter duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections), 1945/1990 history notes, and Dillen v. Remley, 327 S.W.2d 931 (1959) jurisdiction annotation; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked non-signing party defendants and Missouri civil code nonresident service in (1), 20-day return-date hearing limit and denial-only objection scope in (2), and appointment of three sworn disinterested commissioners if objections are overruled in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Tract and parcel definitions and multiple improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12465, A. 1949 S.B. 1084). Covers defining 'tract' and 'parcel' of land for chapter 244 to include town lots or subdivisions by ownership, and clarifying that landowners are not limited to a single ditch, tile, or levee and may construct two or more of each or all three for the same tract.

headings.title: Dismissal when costs exceed benefits and self-funded construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers mandatory dismissal and taxing of court costs against petitioners when the approved or amended commissioners' report shows total costs (including land value, damages, and crossings) exceed total accruing benefits, followed by the right of one or more owners of wet, swamp, flat, or overflowed land to construct at their own expense without taxing other improved landowners.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1949 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked chapter-wide 'tract'/'parcel' town-lot inclusion and multiple-works clarification in (1), and mandatory cost-exceeds-benefits dismissal, petitioner cost taxation, and post-dismissal self-funded construction right without taxing other owners in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Landowner construction right and prior payment of damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12462, A.L. 1945 p. 852). Covers the right of benefitted landowners to construct or arrange construction of the ditch, levee, or tile without circuit court permission, conditioned on paying resulting damages in cash to owners of taken or damaged land or depositing the awarded sum with the circuit clerk before starting construction.

headings.title: Court-let construction contracts, cost apportionment, and liens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers circuit court power, when benefitted owners cannot agree and a majority of interested persons petition after due notice, to let construction to the lowest or best bidder, court-ordered apportionment of total costs by the circuit clerk in proportion to ascertained benefits, and creation of a continuing land lien until paid.

headings.title: Suits to enforce construction cost liens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers enforcing the subsection 2 lien by suit on certified circuit clerk bills brought in the name of the state at the relation of interested parties in any court of competent jurisdiction, with collected sums including court costs and a reasonable court-fixed attorney's fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1945 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked landowner construction right conditioned on prior cash payment or circuit clerk deposit of damages in (1), majority-petitioned court-let contracts, benefit-proportional cost apportionment, and continuing liens upon owner disagreement in (2), and state-relation lien enforcement suits including court costs and court-fixed attorney's fees in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Petitioner cost liability and commissioner and surveyor pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12464, A.L. 1945 p. 852). Covers petitioners' liability for all chapter proceeding costs and sets archived per-diem pay and necessary expenses for commissioners ($2 per day) and surveyors working under commissioners' direction ($3 per day).

headings.title: Special commissioner for court-ordered construction under 244.090
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers circuit court authority when construction becomes the court's duty under section 244.090 to appoint a disinterested special commissioner (who may or may not be a surveyor) to oversee construction, submit progress reports and a final report upon completion, and receive court acceptance and confirmation if performed according to contract.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1945 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked petitioner cost liability and archived $2/$3 per-diem plus expense pay for commissioners and surveyors in (1), and discretionary appointment of a disinterested special commissioner for court-ordered section 244.090 construction with progress/final reports and confirmation in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Amending chapter petitions as other pleadings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12466, A.L. 1945 p. 852). Covers permissive amendment at any time of a petition signed and filed under chapter 244 as other pleadings in other cases.

headings.title: Connecting chapter works to drainage or levee districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers permission for owners of land within or outside a Missouri drainage or levee district to connect chapter-constructed ditches, tiles, or levees with artificial ditches, drains, or levees of a district on terms prescribed by the district's board of supervisors or organizing court.

headings.title: Court sessions for hearing chapter petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers circuit court authority to hear and determine a chapter 244 petition and any related matters at any time during a regular, adjourned, or special session.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1945 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked permissive petition amendment in (1), connecting chapter works to artificial district drains/levees on terms prescribed by district supervisors or organizing court in (2), and circuit court hearing authority at regular, adjourned, or special sessions in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for willfully obstructing or impairing works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12467; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Covers persons, copartnerships, or corporations willfully filling up, obstructing, or impairing chapter-constructed ditches, tiles, or levees, establishing a misdemeanor punishable upon conviction by a $50 to $200 fine per offense or 30 days to 6 months county jail confinement for responsible persons or agents.

headings.title: Entry onto land for surveys after written notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers the right of owners of land to be drained to enter or send an engineer or surveyor onto crossed land without prior consent to take measurements, run levels, and plan works, expressly conditioned on first giving written notice of purpose and intention to the owner of the crossed land.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked willful-conduct mens rea, covered persons/copartnerships/corporations, and misdemeanor fine/jail penalties in (1), and survey entry without consent expressly conditioned on prior written notice to crossed landowners in (2). Retained both drafted headings.
